The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for an amount of Rs.30,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 14.02.2021 at about 6.30 pm., he was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA50Q2124 near Sambram College gate, M S Palya, Bengaluru and at the same time a Innova Crysta bearing reg.No.KA 01AJ1848 being driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against his motor cycle.
As a result, he fell on the ground and sustained SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.1972/2021 grievous injuries all over his body.
Immediately, he was shifted to Aveksha Hospital, Bangalore and took treatment as an inpatient from 14.02.2021 to 22.02.2021.
For further treatment he was shifted to Akasha Hospital, Devanahalli.
He spent sum of Rs.10,00,000/ towards his treatment, medicines, conveyance, nourishment and other charges.
Due to injury he became disabled and lost his earning capacity.
3. Further it is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident he was hale and healthy.
He was working as Security guard and was earning sum of Rs.11,000/ per month and contributing the same towards the maintenance of family.

Further he has stated that the accident occurred due to the negligent on the part of the driver of the Innova Crysta bearing reg.No.KA01AJ1848 and in this regard FIR in crime No.32/2021 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 being the R C owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of Innova Car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, he has prayed to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ from the respondents.
The summons has been duly served on respondent No.1 and 2.
The respondent No.1 has not appeared before this tribunal.
Hence, respondent No.1 has been placed exparte.
The Respondent no.2 has appeared before this tribunal and filed his written statement.
He has contended that he issued commercial vehicle package policy with respect to Toyata Crysta Car bearing Reg. No.KA 01AJ1848 which was valid as on the date of accident.
Further he has contended that his liability is Srinivas.

sentences.text: He has also contended that the owner of the vehicle or the police have not complied with the provisions of IMV Act after the accident.
Further he has denied the entire petition averments as false and baseless.
He has further contended that the driver of the vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Further he has contended that the respondent No.1 knowingly entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having valid and effective driving license as such he committed breach of terms of policy.
He has also contended that the petitioner in collusion with the police have created false documents only to claim exorbitant compensation.

He has also contended that if this tribunal pleases to award any SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.1972/2021 compensation to the petitioner then such compensation amount shall be directed to be deposited directly to the bank account of this tribunal through the process of NEFT and RTGS.
Hence, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following:
:: ISSUES::
1. Whether the Petitioners proves that, on 14022021 at about 06.30 p.m. while petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA50Q2124, when he reached near Sambhrama college gate, MS Palya, Bengaluru city, at that time, the driver of the Innova Crysta bearing Reg. No.KA01AJ1848 drove in the rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner vehicle, as a result of which petitioner sustained grievous injury, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition? If so,
from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
The petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 16 documents as Ex P1 to ExP16.
He has examined Doctor as PW2.
He has got marked 2 documents as Ex.P.17 and Ex.P.18.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.
7. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has not addressed his arguments in spite of sufficient time given to him.
Perused the entire records.

8. My findings to the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

sentences.text: In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner has got examined himself as PW1.
He has got marked 16 documents as ExP1 to ExP16.

He has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed for his SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.1972/2021 examination inchief.
10.
It is relevant to note that the respondent no.2 has specifically denied the very alleged accident and involvement of Toyata Crysta Car bearing reg. No.KA01AJ 1848 in the alleged accident.
Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove the accident and the involvement of said car.

11. PW.1 in his affidavit has stated that on 14022021 at about 06.30 pm he was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA50Q2124 near Sambram College gate, M S Palya, Bengaluru and at that time Innova Crysta Car bearing No. KA01 AJ1848 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against his motor cycle, as a result he fell on the ground and sustained grevious injuries all over his body.

Further he has deposed that in this regard FIR came to be registered in Crime No.32/2021 at Yelahanka Traffic Police station against the driver of the Car for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
12.

The Petitioner in support of his version, he has SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.1972/2021 produced the true copy of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, IMV report,
wound certificates, charge sheet, discharge summary, medical prescriptions, medical bills, advance deposit receipts, medical reports, Xrays, notarised copy of his DL and notarized copy of his ID Card and got them marked at ExP1 to ExP16.
13.
I have perused ExP1 to ExP8.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 1402 2021 at about 06.30 pm., and the FIR in crime No.32/2021 came to be registered on 15022021 at Yelahanka Traffic police station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.

Further the records reveal that thereafter the police conducted investigation and filed chargesheet against the driver of the Innova Car bearing Reg. No.KA01AJ1848 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC.
The IMV report marked at Ex.P.5 reveals that the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicles.
Ex.P.3 - spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 rough sketch reveals that the accident took place on Hessaraghatta main road towards left side of the road.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.1972/2021 PW1.
I have perused the entire crossexamination of PW1.

In his crossexamination he has clearly denied the suggestion that due to his own negligence the accident occurred and not due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Innova car.

sentences.text: On the other hand the Respondent No.2 has not chosen to adduce any evidence to show that the accident had not occurred and the Toyata Innova Car bearing No.KA01AJ 1848 was false implicated in this case.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of driver of the Toyata Innova Car bearing Reg.
No.KA01AJ1848 which belongs to the respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I answer issue SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.1972/2021 No.1 in the affirmative.

15. ISSUE NO.2:
AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME: PW.1 has produced notarised copy of his DL at Ex.P.15.
As per this document, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 0106 1961.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged about 59 years 8 months 13 days.

Therefore, the appropriate multiplier for the said age group as per Sarla Verma's case is '09'.
16.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to accident, he was hale and healthy and working as a Security guard and earning sum of Rs.11,000 to Rs.15,000/ per month.
It is relevant to note that the petitioner in his petition has stated that his income was Rs.11,000/ per month.
In order to show his avocation he has produced Ex.P.16 notarized copy of ID card issued by Pentagon Services.
But this documents does not bear date of issue, validity date or date of birth of petitioner.
The petitioner has not examined the person who has issued this document.
Even he has not adduced any evidence to show his SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.1972/2021 actual income.
Therefore, it is necessary to take into account notional income of the petitioner while calculating the compensation.
Since, the petitioner has himself stated that he was earning Rs.11,000/ per month, the same is taken as notional income while calculating the compensation.
17. PW.1 has deposed that after the accident he was taken to Aveksha Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein,
he took treatment as inpatient from 14022021 to 22022021.
Further he has deposed that thereafter he was shifted to Aakash Hospital, Devanahalli, wherein, he took treatment as inpatient from 02032021 to 12042021.
In this regard he has produced Ex.P.9 - Five discharge summaries.
I have perused the same.
It appears that immediately after the accident the petitioner was taken to Aveksha Hospital and got admitted there till 2202 2021.
Thereafter, it appears that the petitioner was taken to Aakash Hospital, Devanahalli and got treatment as an inpatient from 02032021 to 12042021.

Further this document reveals that the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at Nakshatra Hospital, Devanahalli from 15042021 to 16042021 and again the petitioner got admitted to Aakash Hospital as an SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.1972/2021 inpatient and took treatment from 14072021 to 05082021.

These discharge summaries and wound certificates marked at Ex.P.6 and 7 shows that the petitioner sustained abrasion over top of right and left shoulder, abrasion over back of left and right hand, multiple abrasions over front of right Srinivas.

swelling, tenderness and deformity of right wrist joint, laceration over front of upper and lower part of right knee, laceration over anteromedial aspect of right knee, comminuted displaced fracture of condylar part of lower femur with inter condylar articular extension and surrounding soft tissue swelling, comminuted fracture of inter spinous part of tibia and upper shaft with soft tissue contusion, fracture head and neck of fibula.

sentences.text: Therefore, it indicates that, he took treatment as an inpatient for total period of 75 days.
18. As already stated supra, the Petitioner has examined the Doctor as PW.2 and he has got marked two documents as SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.1972/2021 Ex.P.17 & Ex.P.18.
PW2 has deposed that he subjected the petitioner for assessment of disability clinically and radiologically on 02112022.
Further he has deposed that the petitioner was diagnosed with following injuries 1. Open type III (Rt) side comminuted femoral and Tibial condyle 2.
(Rt) Distal radius.

Further he has deposed that the petitioner underwent following surgeries:
1. Wound debridement + knee spanning Ex.fix for right lower limb under SA +
sedation on 15.02.2021.
2. CRIF with Kwire for right distal radius under brachial block on 15.02.2021.
3.
Ex Fix Removal ORIF with LCP for distal femur and proximal tibia on 26.03.2021.

4. ORIF with plate and screws for right distal redius on 15.04.2021.
5.
Auto logous ilac crest bone grafting for distal femur on 23.07.2021.
6. Implant removal right distal radius on 21.04.2022.

19. PW.2 has further deposed that the Xray of the petitioner taken on 02112022 shows united fractures of distal femur and proximal tibia with implants in situ at both sites and malunited distal radius with regional Osteopaenia.
Further he has deposed that the petitioner is having disability of both limbs at 76% and that of whole body at 38%.
He has also deposed SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.1972/2021 that the petitioner is having disability of right lower limb at 57%.
Further he has deposed that the petitioner requires sum of Rs.50,000/ for removal of implants at both sites in a private sector.
The learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 has cross examined PW.2 but nothing has been elicited from him to disbelieve his version.

20. It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
But in the present case, though PW.2 has assessed disability of Petitioner at 38% as a whole body disability but by looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Srinivas.

sentences.text: Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 25% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
21. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner has undergone pain and sufferings to SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.1972/2021 some extent.
Thus, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.35,000/ under this head.
22. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAIDUP PERIOD:

Considering the age, nature of injuries, treatment given as inpatient in the hospital and as an outpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 6 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.66,000/ (11,000/ x 6) under this head.
23. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
As already stated supra the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for nearly 75 days as it could be seen from Ex.P.5 - discharge summaries.
It is relevant to note that the petitioner has not produced documents to show that he took followup treatment.
Therefore, this tribunal inclines to award Rs.75,000/ under this head.
24. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.10 - medical bills.
The learned counsel for the respondent SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.1972/2021 No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve these documents.
As per these documents, the petitioner had incurred sum of Rs.2,43,253/ towards medical expenses.
Hence, this tribunal awards sum of Rs.2,43,253/ under this head.
25. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '9'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.11,000/ p.m.
Hence, a sum of Rs.2,97,000/ (Rs.11,000 X 12 X 9 X 25/100) is awarded under this head.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face disappointment and frustration & also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures and joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.35,000/ is awarded under this head.
SCCH - 26 17 MVC No.1972/2021 27. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
PW.2 has stated that, Petitioner need sum of Rs.50,000/ to undergo surgery for removal of implants at both sites.
But he has not Srinivas.

N vs Janani Tours And Resorts (P) Ltd on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47863129/
7 given any quotation in this regard.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this tribunal is of the view that in the absence of quotation the Petitioner may incur sum of Rs.25,000/ to undergo surgery for removal of implants.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.25,000/ under the head Future Medical Expenses.

28. The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Pain and sufferings 35,000=00 2 Loss of income during 66,000=00 laidup period 3 Attendant charges, extra 75,000=00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 4
Medical expenses 2,43,253=00 5 Loss of future income due 2,97,000=00 to disability 6 Loss of future amenities & 35,000=00 happiness 7
Future Medical Expenses 25,000=00 TOTAL 7,76,253=00

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,76,253/.
 SCCH - 26 18 MVC No.1972/2021  29.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
30. LIABILITY:
The Respondent No.1 is the owner of offending car and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said car.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.

The primary liability is on respondent No.2 to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till realization.
It is made clear that the Petitioner is not entitled for any interest from the Respondents on future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
31. ISSUE NO.3 :

For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following : :
ORDER :

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
SCCH - 26 19 MVC No.1972/2021 The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,76,253/ (Rupees Seven Lakhs Seventy Six Thousand Two Hundred and Fifty Three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

It is made clear that the Petitioner is not entitled for any interest from the Respondents on future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
